effective_result.title: FHFA Refers Letitia James Mortgage Allegations to DOJ in April 2025
effective_result.description_short: FHFA Refers Letitia James Mortgage Allegations to DOJ on April 14, 2025
effective_result.description_medium: FHFA Director Bill Pulte sent DOJ a referral about New York Attorney General Letitia James's mortgage records on April 14, 2025, ABC News reported. The referral conveyed allegations; it does not establish that they were true. The cited sources do not show a Bondi-directed February investigation or prove retaliation for James's Trump civil-fraud case.
effective_result.description_long:
Federal Housing Finance Agency Director Bill Pulte referred allegations about New York Attorney General Letitia James’s mortgage records to the Justice Department on April 14, 2025. ABC News reported that date from the referral letter and described the allegations about a Virginia property. A referral asks prosecutors to review information; it does not establish that the allegations are true. Later reporting by Reuters said Fannie Mae officials saw no evidence of mortgage fraud in the records discussed in a court filing. That filing was a defense motion and its assertions are advocacy claims, not judicial findings. Reuters also reported that Democratic senators asked the Government Accountability Office to review Trump officials’ conduct in criminal referrals. These developments concern the referral and its oversight; they do not establish why officials acted. The cited sources do not document a Bondi-directed investigation opened in February 2025 or prove that the referral was retaliation for James’s civil-fraud case against Trump. The corrected entry records the April referral and leaves motive unresolved.

The later chronology is distinct from the April referral: a federal grand jury indicted James on October 9, 2025, and on November 24 the court dismissed that indictment without prejudice after finding the interim prosecutor’s appointment invalid. AP later reported that grand juries declined two attempts to re-indict her in December 2025. These were procedural developments, not decisions on the mortgage allegations.

effective_result.title: FEC Records Divided 2022 Votes in Trump Campaign Vendor-Payment Matter
effective_result.description_short: In 2022, the FEC recorded divided votes on Trump campaign vendor-payment disclosure allegations and later closed MUR 7784; it made no criminal-fraud finding against Brad Parscale.
effective_result.description_medium: FEC Matter Under Review 7784 concerned whether Trump campaign committees accurately reported payments to American Made Media Consultants and Parscale Strategy. In 2022, commissioners split 3–3 on whether to find reason to believe certain reporting violations occurred; the Commission later voted 4–2 to close the file. The record does not establish that Brad Parscale committed criminal fraud or personally received $40 million.
effective_result.description_long: Federal Election Commission Matter Under Review 7784 concerned complaints that Trump campaign committees misreported the payees or purposes of payments to American Made Media Consultants and Parscale Strategy. In 2022, the Commission split 3–3 on whether to find reason to believe certain reporting violations occurred, so those allegations did not receive the votes needed for that finding. The Commission later voted 4–2 to close the file. The FEC case page lists the case chronology and statements of reasons dated June 9, June 15, and July 14, 2022; because the cited record does not establish one exact date for the vote sequence in the proposed summary, this account uses year-level dating. The statements show commissioners disagreed and are not a unanimous factual finding. The matter did not establish that Brad Parscale committed criminal fraud or personally pocketed $40 million. This account describes the vendor-payment disclosure dispute and divided enforcement outcome without presenting a complaint, a commissioner’s statement, or reported asset purchases as proof of personal fraud.

effective_result.title: Iran Fires Missiles at Israel After Israel Begins June 2025 Attack
effective_result.description_short: Iran fired its first missiles toward Israel on June 13, 2025, after Israel began strikes on Iran.
effective_result.description_medium: Iran launched missiles toward Israel on June 13, 2025, after Israel began its attack campaign against Iranian targets. Reuters reported that fewer than 100 missiles were fired in the initial barrage and that most were intercepted, according to the Israeli military. The United States struck Iranian nuclear facilities on June 21, after the initial exchange had begun; those later strikes did not trigger the first Iranian barrage.
effective_result.description_long: On June 13, 2025, Iran launched missiles toward Israel after Israel began a campaign of strikes against Iranian nuclear and military targets. Reuters reported that fewer than 100 missiles were fired in the initial Iranian barrage and that most were intercepted or fell short, citing the Israeli military. The United States’ Operation Midnight Hammer struck Iranian nuclear facilities on June 21, after the June 13 initial exchange had begun. Those later U.S. strikes therefore cannot be described as the trigger for the first Iranian barrage. Reuters supports the reported count and immediate sequence, with the count and interceptions attributed to the Israeli military. The Associated Press account of the U.S. operation supports its date and says it followed nine days of Israeli attacks. This entry is limited to the initial reported Iranian missile attack and the later U.S. chronology; it does not summarize the subsequent exchanges or imply that the first barrage ended the conflict.

effective_result.title: Trump Signs Childhood-Vaccine Order and Discusses Autism in August 2026 Remarks
effective_result.description_short: Trump signed a childhood-vaccine order on August 10, 2026, and made autism-related remarks; WHO's review found no causal link.
effective_result.description_medium: On August 10, 2026, President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14420 revising federal childhood-vaccine recommendations, including separate MMR components when available and spacing visits. At the signing, he discussed autism. A WHO review of evidence through 2025 found that rigorous studies do not support a causal association between vaccines and autism. The order and the scientific evidence are distinct.
effective_result.description_long: On August 10, 2026, President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14420, which directs changes to federal childhood-vaccine recommendations, including separate administration of measles, mumps, and rubella components when available and spacing some immunizations across visits. At the signing, Trump discussed autism and childhood vaccination. The executive order documents a policy action and the presidential transcript records his remarks; neither is scientific evidence that vaccines cause autism. The World Health Organization's review of evidence through 2025 found that the most methodologically rigorous studies do not support a causal association between vaccines, including thiomersal-containing vaccines, and autism spectrum disorder. The order was signed by Trump, not by Robert F. Kennedy Jr. This correction therefore changes the event date from 2025 to August 10, 2026, distinguishes the order's recommendations from the president's rhetoric, and separates both from the scientific evidence. It does not treat the signing itself as proof of a vaccine-autism link.

WHO evidence review through 2025: the most methodologically rigorous primary studies do not support a causal association between vaccines and autism spectrum disorder.

effective_result.title: Puerto Rico Adopts Study Estimate of 2,975 Excess Deaths After Hurricane Maria
effective_result.description_short: Puerto Rico adopts study estimate of 2,975 excess deaths after Hurricane Maria
effective_result.description_medium: Puerto Rico adopted a George Washington University study’s estimate of 2,975 excess deaths from September 2017 through February 2018 after Hurricane Maria as its official toll. The estimate compares observed deaths with expected mortality; it does not attribute all deaths to federal decisions. Claims about the administration’s specific response failures or statements require separate evidence.
effective_result.description_long: Puerto Rico commissioned researchers at George Washington University and the University of Puerto Rico to examine mortality after Hurricane Maria. Their study estimated 2,975 excess deaths from September 2017 through the end of February 2018 by comparing observed deaths with the number expected from historical patterns and other demographic factors. Puerto Rico adopted the estimate as the official death toll. The number is an excess-mortality estimate over a defined period, not a list assigning each death to an individual cause or government decision. The study and the university’s statement describe the estimate as deaths after the hurricane; they do not conclude that the Trump administration caused all 2,975 deaths. A separate federal review may address disaster assistance and death-identification efforts, but those subjects are not a substitute for causal evidence about each death. The entry therefore keeps the verified measurement, period, and official adoption together while excluding administration-specific causation that the mortality study does not establish. Claims about an initial federal count, Jones Act timing, or particular aid-distribution failures need their own dated sources. The event remains the revision of Puerto Rico’s official toll following the study, rather than a claim that the estimate apportions responsibility.

supports: The GW/UPR study estimates 2,975 excess deaths from September 2017 through February 2018 using modeled comparisons with expected mortality.
GWU states that the study was commissioned by Puerto Rico, analyzed deaths through February 2018, and estimated 2,975 excess deaths; its method compares observed mortality with expected deaths.
Axios dated its report August 28, 2018, and reported Governor Ricardo Rosselló raised Puerto Rico’s official Hurricane Maria death toll from 64 to 2,975 after a George Washington University study.

GAO reviews federal assistance and selected state and territorial efforts to identify deaths from 2017 hurricanes, including Puerto Rico’s use of the revised Maria toll. It provides response and count context, not an administration-specific causal attribution for all 2,975 deaths.

effective_result.title: Alleged Bondi Directive to Dismiss Unrelated Cases Remains Unsubstantiated
effective_result.description_short: The reviewed sources do not verify a Jan. 21, 2025 directive by Pam Bondi to dismiss unrelated pending cases.
effective_result.description_medium: The staged claim says Attorney General Pam Bondi directed dismissals of unrelated pending cases on January 21, 2025. The reviewed Justice Department page documents President Donald Trump’s January 20 clemency proclamation for January 6-related offenses, a separate action. No cited source establishes the alleged Bondi directive or the claimed dismissals; keep the entry on hold pending a dated DOJ motion, case-specific court docket, or reliable contemporaneous report.
effective_result.description_long: The original entry alleges that Attorney General Pam Bondi directed the Justice Department on January 21, 2025, to dismiss a broad set of unrelated pending cases. The available Justice Department source instead documents President Donald Trump’s January 20 proclamation granting clemency for certain January 6-related offenses. Clemency by presidential proclamation is a distinct actor and action; that page does not substantiate a Bondi directive, DOJ dismissal motions, or the termination of unrelated prosecutions. The existing correction that treated the clemency proclamation as the event would substitute a different event for the unsupported original claim, so this record remains unresolved rather than “corrected.” The exact evidence gap is a dated Bondi directive or case-specific dismissal motions and docket entries, corroborated by reliable contemporaneous reporting. Until that evidence is available, retain this exclusion proposal and do not state the alleged directive as fact.
